raw_response:
*speaking as the farmer*

Ai, another year. These 9 mu, I know them like my own hands — forty years I've worked this land. My back hurts more now, but the work doesn't wait.

My husband helps some, but he's not as strong as he was. My two sons work on construction in the city, they send money but don't touch the fields anymore. My daughter-in-law helps at harvest, that's all. So it's mostly me.

I split my land like always: 6 mu for the wheat-maize, 2 mu cotton on the sandier plot by the west edge, 1 mu mungbean — just a small patch, we eat it, give some to relatives.

**Wheat (6 mu).** Plant after Cold Dew, around October 10. I use the seed I saved from last year's harvest plus a little new seed from the co-op mixed in — full saved seed gets weak after too many years, my neighbor Old Liu told me. Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 bag, 50 jin... no, it's 100 jin now, one bag per mu. Plow it in. When the wheat turns green in spring, around Qingming, I topdress urea — about one bag for every three mu, I scatter it by hand before the water comes. Water twice: winter water in late November before freeze, spring water at jointing. Last year Old Wang skipped spring water to save money and his wheat was thin — I'm not doing that. If I see aphids at heading I'll spray once, maybe 20 yuan a mu. Combine comes around June 8, I pay by the mu.

**Maize (6 mu).** Right after the combine leaves. No time — one week or the season slips. My husband and I rush it, no-till planter hired from the village, cheaper than plowing. Hybrid seed from the agri-shop, the Zhengdan type everyone plants now. At planting I drop half a bag of compound per mu in the row. When maize is knee-high, around late July, I put down urea — half a bag per mu if the leaves look pale, less if they're dark green. The summer rains usually do the watering for me. If July is dry like two years ago, I pump once — costs money, the well water isn't free. Spray once for borer in August. Harvest by hand around National Day, my daughter-in-law helps, we dry the ears on the threshing floor.

**Cotton (2 mu).** On the western plot, sandier soil, too dry for maize to do well there. I plant after Guyu, around April 25, when the ground is warm. Cotton is so much work — picking by hand, bending over all autumn. Price has been poor, but I've grown cotton my whole life, I don't know how to stop. I put a little compound under the row at planting, then urea at first flower. Three sprays at least — bollworm, aphids, sometimes spider mites. One pumping when the bolls are setting if no rain. Picking starts in September, three or four times through November. My daughter-in-law helps in October when it's heaviest.

**Mungbean (1 mu).** Just a patch near the house. I use seed from last year's crop. Scatter after the first good June rain. Doesn't need much — mungbean is tough, that's why grandmother grew it. Maybe a handful of compound per row, no more. One spray if I see bean weevil. Pick by hand in August, dry on a mat. Family eats it all summer in soup.

Total cash out for inputs, I figure about three thousand five hundred yuan. That's the hard part — the fertilizer and seed money comes out before anything comes in. My son sent money at Spring Festival, that covers most of it.
